# 冲突·暴力·危险 {.unnumbered}



> 本主题共 12 篇语境短文。每篇把一批旧词织进一个场景；目标词**加粗**，展开"本篇生词"可遮释义自测。



### The Night the City Burned

The old **feud** between the two gangs had been simmering for years, each side nursing grudges like a slow **bane**. Then one Tuesday the **riot** erupted without warning. A **thug** in a grey hoodie lit the first match — **arson**, pure and deliberate — and the **bang** of shattering glass followed seconds later as a **bomb** gutted the corner pawnshop. Police received a **hoax** call that sent three cruisers to the wrong district, buying the mob precious minutes.

On the rooftop across the street, a **spy** for the eastern crew watched through a scope, relaying positions by radio. Below, **foe** faced **foe** in the narrow alley. One man tried to **spar** with words first — a **spat** over territory that had lasted a decade — but the other answered with a blade and **stab**bed him through the shoulder, enough to **maim** without killing. The victim's scream was swallowed by another **bout** of gunfire as the western faction opened up with whatever **ammo** they had left.

The city's response was swift but savage. A **raid** on the safehouse **rout**ed the remaining fighters; those who resisted were **stun**ned with flashbangs and dragged out. The gang's treasurer, long a **dupe** kept in the dark about the real operations, was **oust**ed from his own hideout and handed to investigators. Evidence showed the crew had used **barb**ed wire and **lash**es to enforce discipline internally — one member had been **slay**n for talking to a reporter. A junior lieutenant confessed to a **duel** that had escalated into something far uglier, a planned **rape** of an entire neighborhood's peace. The **fray** left seventeen injured and two dead.

By dawn the city's **bust** economy had a new wound. The only ones who **rob**bed anything lasting from that night were the cameras — footage that would play on loop for weeks, turning every **terr**orist in the crowd into a face the city would never forget.

### 围城·黑帮·猎局

The **cabal** had been planning for months. At its center stood a former **crook** turned arms broker who carried more **clout** in the underworld than any elected official dared admit. His network stretched from street-level **fraud** rings to shadowy factions rumored to have ties with the **Mafia** — and, if the intelligence files were accurate, even with **Hamas** and the remnants of a **Provo** cell gone dark years ago.

The city felt it first. **Crack**s spiderwebbed across the old ceasefire. A police informant — nothing but a **dupe** lured in by promises of witness protection — vanished overnight; investigators found only a **snare** of false leads where his file used to be. **Decoy** vehicles began circling the district courthouse. Rival factions used **nukes**-grade blackmail material to **expel** the moderate voices from the negotiating table, leaving no one to **deter** the violence that followed. When the shooting started, it **smite** the neighborhood with the force of something almost biblical: storefronts **slashed** open, windows **smashed**, a food truck **smacked** sideways into a hydrant. Three people were **raped** in an alley the cameras no longer covered. Others were **punch**ed unconscious on their doorsteps, their assailants gone before a cry could echo.

By the third day the city was under **siege**. Every **rebel** faction accused the others of **poach**ing turf and turning civilians into **dupes** for their supply runs. A **rival** commander was found **slain** in a parking garage, a **slash** across his throat still wet. The broker himself was **exile**d by his own lieutenants — pushed out quietly, the kind of quiet that is its own **curse**. The whole arrangement had become a **havoc** machine, and no lever remained to stop it. The **sting** of tear gas lingered in the air long after the last shot, a reminder that the only thing harder than surviving a war is explaining afterward who started it.

### When Peace Breaks Down

The **truce** had lasted barely a week. At dawn, a **hitman** hired by a rival faction slipped into the valley under cover of fog, armed not with a **cannon** but with something far quieter. He had been sent to **wreak** havoc before either side could **enlist** new fighters — to **ambush** the supply convoy before it reached the garrison. An **archer** posted on the ridge caught a glimpse of movement below and fired, but the **bullet** from a returning shot sent him tumbling from his perch, leaving a smoking **wreck** of timber and rope behind.

By midday the fragile **breach** in the ceasefire had widened into open **combat**. A **conman** posing as a medic tried to **hijack** a field ambulance; when **compel**led at gunpoint to stop, he confessed he had been working for a **forger** who had spent months **foment**ing distrust between the two camps. Soldiers **assail**ed the forward post with a furious **swipe** of rifle butts and fists. Those who resisted under **duress** were dragged away; two junior officers were found to have been **vying** for the same commander's favour, and one had **usurp**ed the other's rank through blackmail and **extort**ion.

The aftermath was uglier still. Reports surfaced of systematic **caning** of prisoners. A warlord had used the chaos to **abduct** three aid workers, holding them as **trump** cards in a negotiation nobody wanted. Investigators catalogued every **hazard** on site — unexploded ordnance, contaminated water, collapsed shelters — and noted a quiet epidemic of **theft** that had stripped the camp of medicines. One doctor, herself a victim of the violence, said the greatest **hurdle** was not the physical danger but the **incest**uous web of loyalties that made it impossible to **incite** even basic solidarity among survivors. Outside, the **hitman**'s handlers had already vanished, leaving no trail and no conscience.

### Under Fire: A City in Chaos

The coastal city had known **strife** for months. What began as quiet **unrest** — protests, curfews, whispered grievances — had collapsed into something far uglier. Armed **rebels** controlled three districts by dawn, and the government scrambled to **subdue** them before the situation hardened into **anarchy**.

A **sniper** had taken position on the customs-house roof, his crosshairs **stifling** any attempt to advance along the waterfront. Two soldiers tried to **resist** the urge to rush forward; their sergeant ordered them into a shallow **trench** and told them to wait. Someone had clearly tried to **tamper** with the armored vehicle's brakes — a saboteur inside the wire, or perhaps a **snitch** working both sides. A **sleuth** from military intelligence was already on it, piecing together **trojan** malware planted in the base's communications relay the night before.

Meanwhile, at the harbor, **piracy** was the other front. A known **pirate** crew had **kidnapped** a cargo officer and was demanding **ransom** before sunrise. The naval **patrol** boat closed in slowly, its commander careful not to let the kidnappers **muzzle** the negotiations by threatening the hostage. A single miscalculation — a **lethal** burst from the deck gun, a **napalm** drop called in too close — and the hostage was gone. The **menace** the pirates posed was real, but so was the danger of escalation.

Back in the old quarter, an **outlaw** faction was trying to **scotch** the ceasefire talks by distributing weapons. Plain-clothes officers moved to **thwart** them, using **shields** to push through the crowd. One officer was **pummeled** against a wall; another watched a suspect **molest** a civilian to steal his phone, then **snitch** the address of a safe house to rivals across the street. The whole operation threatened to be **stymied** by the sheer speed of events — each move met by a countermove, the city a board no one was winning.

By midday the **assault** on the government quarter was under way. Smoke, shouting, the crack of rifles. Whatever order remained was burning.

### 烽火城下，罪与罚

The **colonel** had spent a lifetime in **martial** service, yet nothing prepared him for the siege that now gripped the city. From the walls, he watched a **phalanx** of enemy soldiers advance under a relentless **barrage** of covering fire, their artillery **bombard**ing the outer fortifications without pause. His orders were clear: **fortify** every remaining gate and hold until the **militia** arrived. The men tightened their **holster**s, locked formation, and waited. A cluster of **missile**s screamed overhead; two **mishaps** with faulty fuses spared the eastern tower, though barely. When the breach finally came, soldiers on both sides began to **grapple** in the rubble — hand to hand, no quarter given. One defender was **impaled** on a broken pike; the wound the battle **inflict**ed on the garrison's morale was no less severe.

By dawn, the enemy had **conquer**ed the lower district. The streets descended into **looting** and **larceny**, merchants stripped of everything they owned. Survivors who **contend**ed with armed gangs were dragged away as **hostage**s, while others — deemed **captive** by circumstance alone — were herded into makeshift pens. Organised **patrols** tried to restore order, but they were too few. A local warlord used the chaos to **oppress** rival clans, his lieutenants quick to **exploit** the power vacuum. Those who dared raise a **protest** were silenced by nightfall.

Behind the lines, a subtler war unfolded. Forgers worked through the night: every document the occupation needed, they would **falsify**, each stamp and signature a fresh act of **forgery**. Agents set out to **defraud** the city's treasury, skimming relief funds meant for the displaced. A **burglar** who had slipped past the curfew was caught mid-job, his **misdeed** trivial against the crimes of those in uniform. A city-wide **manhunt** was launched for the ringleaders, though everyone understood the outcome — whatever victory the occupiers claimed would be **pyrrhic**, the cost in blood and trust far outweighing any ground gained.

### The City Burns

The **warfare** had been grinding on for weeks, but that night the city finally broke. What began as a **quarrel** between two armed factions over a disputed checkpoint escalated within hours into full-scale **rioting**, with crowds surging through the narrow streets while government **corvette**s circled offshore, their searchlights sweeping the waterfront.

By dawn, soldiers moved in to **repulse** the rioters, but the **atrocity** had already been done. They found a **bastille**-like detention centre near the docks whose guards had fled, its cells **battered** open from the outside. The freed prisoners scattered before anyone could determine who among them was a genuine political prisoner and who was merely a **suspect** in a pending **burglary** case. An **assassin** believed to have been **smuggle**d into the city three days earlier was still unaccounted for, and with so much **at stake** the security commander ordered his units to conduct **sorties** into every warehouse district.

The chaos proved to be the **undoing** of the city's provisional governor. A **defector** from the eastern militia revealed, under what his captors called "enhanced questioning" — a euphemism for **torture** that made even hardened officers flinch — that a network of loyalists had been systematically working to **smother** any resistance. They had used **coercion** to silence witnesses, allowed a senior aide to **embezzle** military funds, and sheltered a **traitor** who had handed over the garrison's defence plans. The **calamity** was not accidental: it had been engineered. A squad was dispatched to **ransack** the governor's private offices and **seizure** orders were issued for his assets. Within the hour, soldiers moved to **chastise** the militia commanders who had permitted the breakdown, and military tribunals were convened to **trounce** the ringleaders publicly.

The **conquest** of the old quarter took another two days. A small gang of **cannibal**-cult extremists, barely a dozen strong but capable of extraordinary violence, had **dominate**d a flooded basement shelter, **drowning** their captives if they refused to cooperate. They were finally cornered and subdued, leaving behind evidence of every **warfare**-era crime the prosecutors had feared most.

### The Fortress Falls

The old **fortress** had stood for centuries, but now its walls were **entrenched** with new danger. A **militant** faction had **enlisted** hundreds into its ranks, **regimenting** them under a ruthless chain of command. At the top sat a **sergeant** whose orders were carried out without question — suspects were dragged in **manacles** through the courtyard and **tortured** for intelligence. The **infantry** advanced at dawn, and the first **skirmish** broke out before sunrise. A **landmine** buried beneath the road claimed the first **fatality** of the day; the **headshot** that killed the sentry moments later was the second. What began as a border **flare-up** had spiraled into open **homicide** on a mass scale — some already whispered the word **genocide**.

Behind the lines, a **saboteur** had **tampered** with the army's radio network, **spoofing** command frequencies to sow confusion. His handler used **intrigue** and **hoodwink**ed junior officers into leaking troop positions, putting the entire operation in **jeopardy**. When the general finally discovered the breach, he moved swiftly to **suppress** the leak: the **sabotage** had gone far enough. The **saboteur** was caught, **executed** before dusk, his fate a **tactical** warning to anyone else who might **encroach** on what the command considered sacred ground.

By nightfall, those who had **vanquish**ed the outer perimeter stood among the **trenches**, staring at the smoldering ruin. The **massacre** was over. The war, everyone knew, was not.

### The Long War's Shadow

The **guerrilla** cell had been active for months, each strike calculated to **devastate** civilian infrastructure without triggering a full military response. Their **adversary**—a coalition of regional powers—had grown weary from **attrition**, its **battalion**s stretched thin across three contested corridors. When **Hezbollah** operatives were found to be in **collusion** with a local smuggling network, intelligence chiefs went **ballistic**, demanding that field agents **apprehend** every known **contender** for cell leadership before dawn.

The operation was anything but clean. A van carrying a **homicidal** enforcer rammed a checkpoint in what investigators later called an intentional **collision**; the **explosion** that followed leveled half a block, leaving survivors in a **hazardous** fog of smoke and debris. Two officers caught in the blast were held **in chains** in a basement safe house, their **captivity** designed to **implicate** a rival faction and sow **hostility** between allies. **Espionage** files recovered on-site revealed a years-long **hijacking** of aid convoys—textbook **extortion** dressed up as logistics.

Back in the capital, the **bickering** among ministers had crossed into open **militancy**, with one faction threatening **blackmail** over leaked budget records. A senior official under **detention** agreed to cooperate only after prosecutors promised to limit the charges against him. Investigators were still untangling who had helped **instigate** the original uprising and who bore responsibility for the **brutality** documented in field reports—footage that some officials feared could be spun into propaganda for the next **holocaust** narrative. Every new **intrusion** into the archive, every unauthorized download, narrowed the window for a negotiated exit before the entire peace process collapsed under the weight of its own secrets.

### The City Before It Fell

The **warmonger** general had spent a decade **undermining** the fragile peace, issuing one **ultimatum** after another until the capital's nerve broke. On the night the **rebellion** finally ignited, **bootleggers** and **racketeers** moved freely through the chaos, replenishing **ammunition** caches hidden beneath market stalls. The regime's soldiers, stripped of every moral **safeguard**, began to **slaughter** anyone they found near the checkpoints — yet the crowds kept surging, driven by a hunger for **vengeance** too long deferred.

By dawn the **spearhead** of the insurgency had punched through the northern gate. **Thrashing** the garrison unit in a brutal **scrimmage** outside the courthouse, rebel fighters seized the armory with such speed that the defenders had no time to call in air support. Officers who chose not to **surrender** fled into the old quarter and pulled on civilian **camouflage**, hoping informants would not betray them. Meanwhile, handlers who had once helped the regime **surveil** dissidents now faked new identities, deleting files and **tampering** with surveillance logs to erase their records.

The international observers who arrived at the first **checkpoint** documented every **violation** they could reach: the **torturing** of prisoners in basement cells, the systematic **pilferage** of food and medicine from aid convoys, the **vandalism** of hospitals and schools that bore the scars of deliberate shelling. **Pedophiles** embedded in the militia had used the cover of war to operate unchallenged. **Accomplices** inside the civil service had quietly **persecuted** ethnic minorities for years. **Smuggling** networks — run by the same **racketeers** who had armed both sides — were already adapting, rerouting their operations before the ceasefire ink was dry.

The general, cornered in the palace, issued one last broadcast: he would **retaliate** against any force that crossed the inner wall. His **accomplice** beside him — a man long known to **overthrow** inconvenient legal processes — rehearsed the speech twice before the cameras rolled. **Watch out**, a young interpreter whispered to her colleague; the **truncheon** blows they had taken at the earlier rally had taught them both that words here still carried real weight.

### When the Smoke Clears

The **conspiracy** had been forming for months in the city's underbelly — a web of **complicity** so thick that even seasoned **gangbuster**s struggled to untangle it. At its center stood a **tyrannical** crime lord who **intimidate**d witnesses, **perpetrate**d extortion, and relied on a network of **conspirator**s to keep his operations invisible. His lieutenants dealt in **counterfeit** documents, **clandestine** meetings, and **fraudulent** contracts that bled the city's treasury dry.

The **insurgency** his rivals launched against him triggered open **belligerent** street conflict. The first night of fighting brought **bombardment** of two rival warehouses — fire **smothering** the exits before anyone inside could flee. Whole neighborhoods faced the **disruption** of supply lines and communications; local infrastructure was nearly **obliterate**d in the crossfire. A **catastrophe** seemed inevitable as each faction threatened to **cannibalize** the other's turf, stripping it bare of anything useful. One **altercation** in the market square left three men dead and **jeopardize**d a fragile ceasefire the district council had spent weeks negotiating. A **subversive** pamphlet, found scattered across the rubble, accused the council itself of **appeasement** — choosing cowardice over justice.

It fell to an **undercover** detective to **transgress** the syndicate's inner circle. Working alone, she exposed the **oppression** the crime lord imposed through debt and **confinement** — holding debtors in basement cells until their families paid. She caught his chief **persecutor** **red-handed**, mid-operation, filing a **preemptive** raid report to corrupt officers before she could act. Her **contention** — that dismantling the network required prosecuting every link in the chain, not just the top — finally prevailed. When the arrests came, they were swift and total, leaving no room for the syndicate to regroup.

### Under Siege

The city had been under **surveillance** for weeks before the **confrontation** erupted. A **conspiratorial** network — funded through **embezzlement** of public relief funds — had spent months preparing. Their **premeditation** showed in every detail: safe houses, false papers, **counterfeits** of official passes.

The **provocateur** at the center of the plot was a veteran of **infiltration** operations, skilled at spreading **provocation** until ordinary men raised their fists. His methods relied on **intimidation** rather than open force, tightening a **stranglehold** on the district's leadership before anyone noticed the **entanglement**. Charges of **misdemeanor** were his preferred camouflage; the graver work — **persecution** of dissenters, the quiet **exploitation** of the desperate — was buried beneath layers of **disobedience** blamed on rival factions.

When the authorities finally moved, the ring's **perpetrator** tried to **outmaneuver** them using **strategical** withdrawals through the port's **minesweeping** lanes, counting on **obstruction** at every checkpoint to buy time. But the **retaliation** came fast. Courts documented each **transgression**, from juvenile **delinquency** recruited into the network, to the attempted **assassination** of a magistrate, to the wholesale **destruction** and **devastation** left in the wake of the final raid. The accused offered **repudiation** of every charge; the evidence offered **anti-Semitic** pamphlets, weapons caches, and a paper trail of **draft dodger** payments that made denial impossible. What had begun as a shadowy **exploitation** scheme ended in the most complete legal reckoning the district had seen in a generation.

### When the City Turns Dangerous

The investigation had been months in the making. Authorities suspected a mid-level official of **misappropriating** public defense funds — quietly siphoning money meant for the city's security infrastructure. Before any arrest could be made, the task force launched a covert **reconnaissance** of his known associates, mapping warehouses and safe houses on the waterfront where **drug trafficking** networks operated under the cover of shipping logistics.

Then things turned ugly. Someone inside the unit leaked the operation. The official's allies moved swiftly to **screw the lead detective over**, planting forged records and launching a vicious **smear campaign** against her in the press. She had expected retaliation — **whistleblowing** never came without a cost — but the speed and viciousness of it still caught her off guard. For weeks she **was subjected to** anonymous threats, surveillance, and public humiliation.

Down at the harbor, the network's recruiters worked a different angle. They would **lure wayward sailors** — men adrift, broke, and desperate — into the operation with promises of easy money, cycling them into courier routes before the men even understood what they had signed on to. The youngest catches were barely teenagers, their cases eventually handed off to a juvenile court already overwhelmed with **juvenile delinquency** filings from the same neighborhoods.

The city's rot ran deep, and everyone who tried to cut it out bore the scars.
